constants.note: exact SI (2019); F = N_A e and R = N_A k_B

conventions.activity: a = c/c°, c° the registry's standard_concentration_mM (1000 mM)
conventions.potential: μ̃ = μ° + RT ln a + z F φ_e; ΔG_m = Σ ν_{s,e} μ̃_{s,e}
conventions.rates: α = k0 Π a_{s,e}^order exp(ζ ψ), ψ = F (φ_N − φ_P)/RT; ζ_fwd − ζ_bwd is the charge an edge moves N -> P
conventions.cycles: a cycle's edges carry +1 (from -> to) or −1 in its + direction; ν is the change of each row per + cycle
conventions.host: a population's host is a patch with ends a (its cell) and b (the outside node), V = φ_a − φ_b; orientation names the host end that is N
conventions.factored: J = k a S (1 − e^{ΔG/RT}); J⁺ = k a S, J⁻ = J⁺ e^{ΔG/RT}
conventions.diagram: S_κ = j⁺_κ/ω with j±_κ = Π±_κ Σ_κ/Σ per carrier (1/s) and ω the law's rate_scale_per_s; k = N_carriers ω
conventions.net_flow: J_m = a Σ_t k_t (1 − exp(ΔG_t/RT + ε_t ψ))
conventions.binding: forms carry integer ligand counts relative to their binder's base form; ligand rows hold total equivalents counted from the base forms
conventions.synthetic: every constant and range is this package's own, D152 §2.4

registry.note: Seam A's registry. ATP, ADP and Pi are neutral transformed rows (FR-4's convention), so Δ_rG'°/RT = 0.4 − 0.3 − 12.0 = −11.9 per hydrolysis. Every value is synthetic (D152 §2.4).

laws.note: D1: one cycle, an electrogenic ATP-driven pump moving 2 H+ N -> P
D2: a 6-state exchanger, 3 X+ in for 1 Y2+ out, with a slip edge (the empty carrier crossing): three Hill cycles that share edges
D3: two cycles sharing only a state (an X+ uniport and a neutral Z uniport): the admitted basis, which is the full set
D4: parallel branches between two states (one co-transports H+), giving three Hill cycles; the 2-cycle K3 is the branches' slip
COMPARTMENT_PH_TRANSFER_DESIGN §6: J = k a S (1 − e^{ΔG/RT}), S = [1 + (K_H/h_N)^n]^-1 [1 + K_ATP/c_ATP]^-1, N the inside (fuel) end
R-fuel's statement (validation/compartment_ph/REFERENCES_USAGE.md): §6's form with a neutral solute (here Z) in place of H+ and no voltage term
R-fuel's statement (validation/compartment_ph/REFERENCES_USAGE.md): §6's form with a neutral solute (here Z) in place of H+ and no voltage term
PLANTED: the neutral law with S − 0.05, negative wherever S < 0.05; the kind must refuse those states
PLANTED (net-flow mode): J = k (1 − exp(ΔG/RT + 0.2 ψ)), an effective charge 1.2 against the mode's 1, booked in the 3:1 stoichiometry. J ΔG > 0 in the band between ΔG = 0 and ΔG/RT = −0.2 ψ

PLANTED (net-flow mode): fb_shift's exchange beside an admitted X+ leak 50 times its capacity. The exchange runs against its ΔG in the band, but the population's total stays dissipative: the guard cannot see it

CONTROL (net-flow mode): the cycles A, B and C = A − B booked in the basis {A, B}, as J_A + J_C and J_B − J_C with each J_x = k_x (1 − e^{ΔG_x/RT}). A mode runs against its own ΔG at some states while Σ J ΔG ≤ 0 everywhere: the guard must not fire

AMENDMENT 1: the neutral law on finite fuel rows (finite_fuel_rows@1): ATP, ADP and Pi are moved at N = a, nothing is held, and the stored rate is the moved rows' standard part, RT (Σ ν μ°/RT − (Σ ν) ln c°) per cycle (§3.4)
AMENDMENT 1: D2 with N = b (the outside node as N); its host states are the exchange family's with the ends swapped

registry.note: Seam C's registry: binder rows hold totals at their base form's valence; ligand rows hold total equivalents counted from each base form. A form's charge is z_base + Σ n z_L. pi2_PO4 sits below its base (a count of −1), admitted by §19 item 6. Every constant is synthetic (D152 §2.4).

S1.note: one ligand and one binder (B4's case)

S3.note: two ligands on one binder, with a form holding both

S4.note: two ligands, three binders, a form below its base (pi2_PO4)

S5.note: two disjoint ligand sets at one node

S6.note: three ligands connected through shared binders

S7.note: amendment C4: a binder whose Mg²⁺ binding releases H⁺, so the per-ligand floors are not the joint condition

P1a.note: a buffered outside node: 40 mM of a pK 7.0 buffer at pH 7.2

P1b.note: the same draw from a node holding H+ and Mg2+ under one closure

movers.note: MgATP moved as its base form and its ligand
PLANTED: a form moved as if it were a row
PLANTED: a mover of a multi-form row that declares no forms

E0_b4.note: one ligand and one two-form buffer: the general lag must equal B4's formula

E1_chain.note: the cooperative chain: its slowest mode is slower than every single step; the true lag is outside the 1e-3 pH budget while a per-step minimum puts it inside

E1_chain_small.note: E1_chain at a tenth of the drive: the kinetic lag meets the first order at second order

E1_chain_kon10.note: E1_chain with every k_on ten times larger: the lag falls tenfold

E1_chain_kon100.note: E1_chain with every k_on a hundred times larger: the closure is the limit

E1_chain_two_drives.note: E1_chain driven in both ligands: the Mg²⁺ steps and the coupling through the base

E2_nuc4.note: a two-ligand binder without a bottleneck: a per-step minimum is conservative here

E2_nuc4_binder_drive.note: E2 with its binder's base form moved in (a moved binder row)

envelope.note: amendment C3: k_on per (binder, ligand); drives on free ligands or a binder's base form; record times in units of the network's slowest relaxation time

validity.note: amendment C4: t* = min over the ligand simplex of λ·T − Σ_B T_B min_f λ·n_f; a state is valid iff t* > 0; the per-ligand floors are t at λ = e_L

boundary.note: t* = 0: on the boundary, not interior

feasible_near.note: t* = +1/2: valid, close to the boundary
